Three governance priorities: real-time accounting/transparency, cross-party dialogue and active listening/citizen participation. Unique-party transparency and anti-corruption effect claims are source assertions.

Social/environment priorities: universal rights, migrant regularisation initiative, youth/self-employed care, social-purpose economy, ecological transition and peace. Signature/beneficiary totals and promised benefits are not independently certified.
Raquel Torrejón presidency candidate and Jorge Serrano Senate head biographies. Past municipal campaign results/volunteer histories are not programme positions.

Measures 1-3: real-time party/State accounting, party asset liability for corruption/illegal funding, suspend representative/high party official upon criminal charge and resign on final conviction. Charge and conviction thresholds are distinct.

Measures 4-11: judiciary council thirds from Parliament, judge associations and unaffiliated judges; programme two-thirds fulfilment contract, independent oversight, five-year sector cooling-off. Respect code, cross-party dialogue, restorative justice and reconciliation museums; no parliamentary-vote equivalence inferred.

Measures 12-13: easier citizen initiatives/referendums and limit legislative postponements. Campaign caption/signature counts and suspended-law examples are source background, not completed laws or exact new limits.

Measures 14-16: finance parties partly by votes not only seats; candidate endorsement threshold 0.1% to 0.05% electorate. Understandable public transparency portals and direct-member elections for specified party offices/candidates. No fully specified seat-allocation reform.

Measures 17-19: treaty human-rights obligations, international resolution follow-up committee and new official-secrets law excluding human-rights violations from secrecy. Citations to civil-society authors are explicitly adopted proposals, not automatic inheritance to other parties.

Measures 20-29: arms export risk/parliamentary control, anti-racism; public universal healthcare regardless legal status, staff/primary/mental health and drug prevention. Universal refundable child tax aid, 24-week birth/adoption leave and at least four months paid parental leave per parent are distinct. Free specialised early intervention ages 0-6; child-violence specialised courts begins and continues.

Completes measure 29 child protection. Measures 30-35: deinstitutionalisation, no residential child placement ages 0-6 with foster priority, comprehensive care and national palliative guarantees, disability social one-stop office. Housing-law support expressly includes rent limits in specific situations and public housing/rehabilitation; expand co-housing/public-private models. Not every rent universally capped.

Measures 36-41: mortgage/consumer protections and dation especially for vulnerability; homelessness prevention/urgency and state shanty-housing fund with sustained family support. Prison staffing/employment reintegration and digital access with restrictions; not unrestricted prison internet.

Measures 42-44: stable consensual education pact, development-appropriate affective-sexual and mandatory rights/democracy/peace/environment/gender education; family/community participation and State minima. Strengthen free inclusive public school availability; demographics are source background.

Measures 45-52: coexist public/private/concerted school, increased concert funding conditioned on no family tuition and inclusion; universal 0-3 education through grants/social tariffs, not universal free wording. Disability-inclusive education, teacher practical/pedagogical/psychological assessment, vocational law/dual training incentives and grants, free public university and culture law.

Measures 53-60: cultural communication; universal unconditional basic income over three years, gradually subject to State capacity. Gradual 35-hour week, original page visually resolves native 3 5 artifact; salary maintenance not specified. Employment agency, constitutional public-pension protection/purchasing power, extraordinary migrant regularisation and border/asylum/child rights, no hot returns and child-centred reception.

Measures 61-69: close migrant detention centres, humanitarian asylum extension, consular capacity/safe migration/sea rescue and migrants social/political/cultural rights. Gender equality, prostitution abolition plus alternative dignified work/support, anti-trafficking; no detailed criminal mechanism specified.

Measures 70-77: gender-violence third-sector participation/orphan support, maintain surrogacy prohibition with vulnerability rationale, feminised-poverty measures. Unwanted-pregnancy prevention and vulnerable-pregnant support; right to pre/post-abortion psychological support is not compulsory counselling or abortion prohibition. LGTBI rights/development-appropriate school diversity.

Measures 78-83: State/regional student-worker funds for unsupported students with one month contributions in previous year, grant/rental-room requirements, foreign placement fairness, youth jobs/mental-health and youth housing-law resources. Youth unemployment figure is party-era background.

Measures 84-89: poverty pact/minimum common social-service floor, expand minimum-income coverage/amount and flexible household criteria/poverty threshold. School-meal access for children in poverty, energy as social right with price-setting/regulation intervention and efficiency, culture for excluded groups; no specified meal fee or energy tariff.

Measures 90-96: self-employed/SME guarantee loans/advice/rural startup, European fiscal reform toward company parity, real-income contribution bands with targeted bonuses, general-regime contribution-gap parity and eliminate duplicate multiple-activity contributions. One-month State payment deadline with sanctions; current effective-tax/repayment figures unverified.

Measures 97-106: more anti-fraud resources/reverse corporate-tax decline and higher SICAV burden; foreign-income difference tax mechanism, remove banknotes above 100 euros and transparent ownership registry. Territorial coordination/solidarity, third-sector voice/CES participation and national volunteering strategy. Policy effect claims not guaranteed.

Measures 107-113: stable national third-sector financing, social-economy law/strategy, insertion-to-ordinary work pathways, favour social-economy procurement, circular/local economy and public science/strategic sectors. Science/innovation target 3% GDP, no fiscal period specified or success guarantee.

Measures 114-116: eliminate fossil-energy sources within maximum three decades, State regulation/ecological incentives and local self-consumption. Responsible consumption/rural services/repopulation/agrarian innovation; discourage imports lacking minimum labour/environment standards, not all imports.

Measures 117-123: stricter animal cosmetics/circus/popular-festival regulation and ban production-efficiency overcrowding; not blanket livestock abolition. Biodiversity protected areas with rural needs, ethical EU/external peace policy, global multinational minimum tax 25% and fair developing-country proceeds, climate/Agenda2030/cooperation. Development aid 0.7% gross national income in 2030; 10% of that aid humanitarian, not 10% national income.

Measures 124-125: AECID budget at least 2,000 million (period not separately specified) and stronger official/development-NGO cooperation/resources/volunteering. Ends the 125 measures, no additional scored proposal inferred from external organisations.

Bibliography introduction explicitly says about 30 measures adopted from named civil-society proposals. Directly adopted cited measures may ground this programme; never inherit every cited organisation proposal or another party stance.
